papers.title_in_file: Quantum reservoir computing in Jaynes-Cummings models: Nonlinear memory and time-series prediction
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of quantum reservoir computing with a driven, dissipative qubit-boson Jaynes-Cummings system and its dispersive limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in the short-term memory and parity-check tasks, the reservoir has a very limited memory of the injected input sequences for linear tasks but a fairly good memory for nonlinear tasks.
quotes: we demonstrated that the reservoir has a very limited memory of the injected input sequences for linear tasks but a fairly good memory for nonlinear tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that for autonomous generation of the Mackey-Glass series the JC and DJC models gave comparable performance with optimum RMSE values in the range 10% < RMSE < 22%, and that for 1-step forecasting they reached a minimum RMSE of approximately 1%.
quotes: the JC and DJC models yielded comparable performance with optimum RMSE values in the range 10% < RMSE < 22%
for 1-step forecasting, we achieved a minimum RMSE of approximately 1%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state they used a local master equation with only bosonic spontaneous decay, assuming weak coupling between the qubit and the mode, and that they did not include an effective qubit decay induced by cavity dissipation in the dispersive limit.
quotes: We have chosen to work with a local master equation with only bosonic spontaneous decay, under the assumption of weak coupling between the qubit and the mode
In this work we have not included this effect
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Discussion, p.12.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum RNNs and LSTMs Through Entangling and Disentangling Power of Unitary Transformations
papers.what_it_is: A framework that models a quantum LSTM cell with system and ancilla registers, reading entangling and disentangling power of unitaries as memory retention and forgetting, with small simulations.

assertions.value: The paper proposes a quantum LSTM model in which entanglement between system and ancilla registers encodes temporal memory, and the authors interpret entangling and disentangling power as information retention and forgetting mechanisms.
quotes: we interpret entangling and disentangling power as information retention and forgetting mechanisms in LSTMs
we have described a quantum LSTM model in which the entanglement between system and ancilla registers directly encodes temporal memory
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The paper argues that the change in ancilla entropy is bounded by the entangling and disentangling power of the unitary.
quotes: The bound on the change of entropy can be understood through the entangling and disentangling power of unitaries
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report simulations on 100 noisy sine values with 80% of the data for training and 20% for testing, and on 365 days of Ontario weather data, and state that the model is mostly able to predict the expected values.
quotes: first creating 100 values in the range
80% for training and 20% for testing
We have also taken 365 days of weather data between 10 May 2024 and 10 May 2025 for Ontario, Canada
As seen from both figures, the model is mostly able to predict the expected values.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Evidence is two small simulations; the fit is shown only in figure images, with no classical baseline in the text read.

papers.title_in_file: From Theory to Practice: Analyzing Variational Quantum Power Method for Quantum Optimization of QUBO Problems
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical and simulation study of the variational quantum power method with qubit locking for QUBO problems, compared with QAOA.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulations from n = 4 to n = 16 qubits QAOA with p = 8 dropped from a success probability of 0.70 at n = 4 to 0.18 at n = 16, while VQPM held an average target state probability between 0.35 and 0.46 across most sizes.
quotes: Even the deepest tested configuration (p = 8) exhibits a sharp drop from 0.70 at n = 4 to 0.18 at n = 16.
maintaining a stable average target state probability hovering between 0.35 and 0.46 across most sizes
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the scaling comparison used 10 trials per step on randomly sampled QUBO instances, and that VQPM ran under a restricted maximum of 30 iterations with a static threshold pdiff = 0.01.
quotes: evaluated over 10 trials per step
operating under a restricted maximum of 30 iterations and a static threshold (pdiff = 0.01)
assertions.certainty_reason: Fig. 10 caption and text, p.13.

assertions.value: The authors report that in a noisy Qiskit Aer simulation of a 12-qubit QUBO problem with 100,000 shots per qubit measurement, VQPM locked only 9 out of 12 qubits and converged to a suboptimal energy of -23.0683 against the noiseless optimum of -26.7515.
quotes: The algorithm locked only 9 out of 12 qubits within the maximum iterations
converged to a suboptimal solution with energy -23.0683, compared to the optimal -26.7515 found by the noiseless simulation
100,000 shots per qubit measurement
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: A single instance (one random seed), so it shows a failure mode and not a rate.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid model of the kernel method for quantum computers (Portuguese text with English abstract)
papers.version_note: The file is the Portuguese-language journal article (R. Bras. Fis. Tecnol. Apl., v.9 n.1, 2022) with an English abstract; the record's English title matches it. The arXiv id in the file name is 2410.23315.
papers.partial_detail: Portuguese methods, results and conclusions skimmed; English abstract read in full. Accented Portuguese passages were not quoted.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical kernel classifier with a quantum inner-product circuit, tested in an ideal Qiskit simulator on a circle-in-square classification task.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid kernel method classified 99% of new random points correctly, 100% inside the circle and 98% outside, with the learned circle slightly larger than the one used to generate the labels.
assertions.anchor: Results (Portuguese text) and English abstract, pp.59-61
quotes: It was found that the algorithm was able to correctly detect new points in 99% of the samples tested, with a small difference due to considering the radius slightly larger than the ideal.
99% dos pontos foram classificados corretamente. Mais especificamente, 100% dos pontos no interior e 98% dos pontos no exterior foram classificados corretamente.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the proposal is a hybrid learning method based on classic kernel methods, with a new quantum algorithm for the inner product between vectors of continuous values, tested on a single toy classification case.
quotes: a hybrid learning method based on classic kernel methods is proposed

As a test case, we applied this new algorithm to learn to classify whether new points generated randomly, in a finite square located under a plane, were found inside or outside a circle located inside this square.
assertions.certainty_reason: English abstract, p.61.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum computing applications in High Energy Physics: clustering, integration and generative models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract area, Chapter 7 outlook and final remarks, and the Spanish summary skimmed; chapters 4 to 6 not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A doctoral thesis on quantum algorithms for particle-physics clustering, Feynman-loop integration (QFIAE) and generative modeling of fragmentation functions.

assertions.value: The thesis states that its quantum K-means design offers exponential speedups in vector dimensionality d and number of clusters K on quantum hardware with qRAM, that its quantum kT-jet clustering improves the runtime from O(N 3) classically to O(N 2 log N ) quantumly, and that its quantum simulations showed clustering efficiencies comparable to classical methods.
quotes: offering exponential speedups in vector dimensionality d and number of clusters K when executed on quantum hardware with qRAM
improves the runtime from O(N 3) classically to O(N 2 log N ) quantumly
our quantum simulations demonstrated clustering efficiencies comparable to classical methods
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedups assume qRAM and a fault-tolerant machine; the accuracy results come from simulation.

assertions.value: The thesis reports that its QFIAE quantum integrator achieved a relative error of about 1% on a one-dimensional scattering process, and reached errors around 5% for tadpole integrals run on Qibo and IBM Quantum computers.
quotes: QFIAE achieved a relative error of about 1% with circuits that remain within the depth and width limits of current NISQ devices
we successfully ran the full algorithm in the quantum computers of Qibo and IBM Quantum for tadpole integrals, reaching errors around 5%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The thesis states that significant progress is still required in hardware, where better quantum processors must be built, and in software, where more efficient and resilient algorithms are needed to achieve quantum advantage.
quotes: Nevertheless, significant progress is still required. Both in hardware, where better quantum processors must be built, and in software, where more efficient and resilient algorithms are needed to achieve quantum advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: Chapter 7, p.110.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Real-World Finance: Scalable Solutions for Dynamic Portfolio Optimization Problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methods summary, conclusion; numerical sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A VQE workflow with a post-processing routine (ISQR) and a problem-splitting variant (VQEC) for dynamic portfolio optimization, run on IBM Fez with up to 38 assets.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results on a real IBM Fez QPU show the tailored workflow achieves financial performance on par with classical methods, with optimized results comparable to those of the CPLEX classical optimizer.
quotes: Our results, obtained on a real Quantum Processing Unit (IBM Fez), show that this tailored workflow achieves financial performance on par with classical methods
This consistent performance yields optimized results that are comparable to those obtained by the CPLEX classical optimizer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that for a 9-asset problem in one investment window some ISQR solutions, including the best one, surpass a Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR) of 1.68%, while the CPLEX solution does not.
quotes: Most importantly, some of the ISQR solutions, and specifically, the best performing solution (dark blue dot), surpass the MARR threshold.
the solution obtained with the IBM Decision Optimization CPLEX [34] classical optimizer (yellow diamond) does not surpass the MARR threshold
We also include a Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR) of 1.68%
obtained for a 9-asset problem at a specific investment window
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: One 9-asset instance in one window; not evidence of general superiority.

assertions.value: The authors state that the VQEC approach does not allow simultaneous exploration of strategies that reduce transaction costs across the full portfolio, and that they acknowledge there is still room for improvement.
assertions.anchor: Section III and Section VI, pp.6, 12
quotes: Note that this approach does not allow for the simultaneous exploration of strategies that reduce transaction costs across the full portfolio.
While the current demonstration is robust, we acknowledge that there is still room for improvement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III (VQEC description) and Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum machine learning framework for longitudinal biomedical studies
papers.what_it_is: A modified IQP quantum feature map that encodes temporal dependencies, tested in simulation on synthetic data and two small public biomedical datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the longitudinal IQP feature map consistently showed improved test performance relative to the IQP feature map on the follicular lymphoma and Alzheimer's disease datasets (test counts are in Table I, not quoted here).
assertions.anchor: Section V and Table I, p.4
quotes: the longitudinal IQP feature map consistently demonstrates improved test performance relative to the IQP approach
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The test sets are very small, so the difference rests on a handful of subjects.

assertions.value: The authors state that the follicular lymphoma task classifies 32 subjects into two groups and that the Alzheimer's disease dataset holds 150 subjects.
quotes: we consider the task of classifying 32 subjects into two groups
The data of 150 subjects is present with a longitudinal collection of 3 or 4 individual MRI scans.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV, p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains challenging to find a public dataset with a big enough cohort to evaluate generalization, that results for all feature maps may benefit from additional hyperparameter tuning, and that near-term quantum models may remain classically simulable.
quotes: it remains challenging to find a public dataset with big enough cohort size to evaluate the generalization capabilities of the proposed model
the results for all feature maps, including RBF, may benefit from additional hyperparameter tuning
Even if near-term quantum models remain classically simulable
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V Discussion, p.4.

papers.title_in_file: eQMARL: Entangled Quantum Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Distributed Cooperation over Quantum Channels
papers.what_it_is: A distributed actor-critic framework for quantum multi-agent reinforcement learning with a quantum entangled split critic, tested in simulation on CoinGame, CartPole and MiniGrid.

assertions.value: The authors report that eQMARL converges to a cooperative strategy 10.8% faster with a higher score than sCTDE in the MDP setting, and 17.8% faster with slightly higher score than qfCTDE in the POMDP setting.
quotes: For MDP, we have shown that eQMARL converges to a cooperative strategy 10.8% faster and with a higher score compared to sCTDE.
for POMDP, we have shown that eQMARL converges to a cooperative strategy 17.8% faster and with slightly higher score compared to qfCTDE
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that eQMARL requires 25-times fewer centralized parameters than sCTDE.
quotes: Lastly, we have shown that eQMARL requires 25-times fewer centralized parameters compared to sCTDE.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or authors' own result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they assume an ideal quantum channel with no losses, and that a limitation is the computational complexity of simulating quantum circuits on classical hardware.
quotes: we assume an ideal quantum channel environment with no losses
One limitation of this work is the computational complexity of quantum simulations on classical hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 (channel assumption) and Section 4 (limitation).
